neighbours.label: the adverbs ' almost' and ' actually' (and imperative ' See'): a hedge or emphasis word before the thing it qualifies
fire: By the end of the race the runners had covered almost forty kilometers.
Our neighbor told us that the old oak tree is actually hollow inside.
The ticket price went up to almost double what it cost last year.
If you look closely, the painting is actually signed in the corner.
Questions about delivery are common. See the shipping page for details.
The museum guide said the statue was actually carved from a single stone.
The temperature dropped to almost zero on the first night of camping.
Many people assume the spider is dangerous, but it is actually harmless.
quiet: By the end of the race the runners had covered nearly forty kilometers.
Our neighbor told us that the old oak tree is hollow inside.
The ticket price went up to roughly double what it cost last year.
If you look closely, the painting is signed in the corner by the artist.
Questions about delivery are common. Visit the shipping page for details.
The museum guide said the statue was carved from a single block of granite.
The temperature dropped to around zero on the first night of camping.
Many people assume the spider is dangerous, but it is really harmless.
